Red dots indicate adjusted P-val < 0.01, black dots indicate adjusted P-val >= 0.01.

"Up regulated" means positive logFC (above 0). So I need to look at the upper portion of each cluster column (positive logFC values) and count red dots.

Let me look at each cluster. Cluster 8 (the olive/green colored column) appears to have a very dense column of red dots in the positive logFC region, extending from about 0 up to ~2 with many red dots. Cluster 5 also has many red dots in positive region. Cluster 8 looks the densest with a thick vertical band of red dots above 0.

Let me look carefully. In panel H, cluster 8 column shows a dense tall cluster of red dots spanning from ~0 to ~2+ in the upper half. Cluster 5 also has a fairly tall red band but maybe less dense. Cluster 8's red band looks the tallest and densest in the up-regulated (positive) side.

Comparing options: 1, 8, 6, 4, 3, 7, 2. Among these, cluster 8 clearly has the most red dots in the positive logFC region.

Thus answer is B (8).

Let me double check cluster 8: yes there's a thick vertical red stripe. Cluster 5 also thick but 5 not in options. Among options, 8 is the clear winner.

Therefore answer B.
